sections.overview: Triplofusus giganteus, the horse conch, is a large predatory marine gastropod of the western Atlantic and Gulf of Mexico region.
sections.identification: Its robust shell can exceed 50 cm, and younger shells are often orange; the living animal has a vivid orange-red foot.
sections.habitat: It occurs in shallow marine waters from North Carolina to the Yucatán Peninsula.
sections.diet: It preys on other large sea snails, including lightning whelks and tulip snails.
sections.behavior: It uses its muscular foot to envelop and smother prey.
sections.reproduction: Females lay distinctive fan-shaped capsules of eggs.
sections.ecology: As a large predator, it is part of coastal food webs and its shell is also heavily sought by collectors.
sections.conservation: A population study reports declines associated with long-term shell collecting and commercial harvest, alongside coastal development.
